nvr.basis: Orders (Norce, Babyshop + Lekmer) matched to their GA4 purchase session; channel = the session's source/medium (GA4 session attribution). New = customer's first order (Norce first-order flag). Counts are scaled up by each market's match rate before cost per new customer = Funnel de-duplicated spend ÷ new customers. The last ~2 days are still settling (lower match rate).
unavailable: Lekmer: none of its orders match a GA4 session in fct_order_ga4_match, so new vs returning by channel cannot be split for it.

notes: GP2 margin basis (Meta scoring, GP3, channel marginal): pacing's Norce model (merchandise − BC returns − BC COGS rate − shipping-model cost: pick & pack, freight) applied to Funnel channel revenue; Funnel's own GP2 is the fallback, labelled per row. Google's profit ROAS stays platform-reported: its conversion value is Babyshop's own profit definition, not this GP2.

Platform-reported: Google ROAS = profit ÷ spend (conversion value is PROFIT in the Babyshop accounts); tROAS is on the same profit basis. Last 1–3 days are still filling in (conversion lag), so judge campaigns on L14, not yesterday.

Google has no budget: spend is context, judged by incremental GP3. Google spend = Funnel de-duplicated SEK cost through yesterday; today = live API spend × Norce FX. Babyshop SE/NO/FI/DK/ROW + Lekmer SE/NO/DK accounts. Any campaign limited by budget is flagged as an error.
Lekmer has no Meta ad account in the warehouse (only Babyshop's, 2927326560764919), so Meta rows are Babyshop only. The approved 200 k Meta plan is Babyshop's.

Marginal profit ROAS (Google) comes from the ROAS-Simulations curves, κ-calibrated (v_kappa_calibrated; λ slope gate not applied): the extra profit per krona from a 10 % lower tROAS ('down'), and what the krona cut by a 10 % higher tROAS earned ('up'). Campaigns without a curve fall back to a 28-day spend/profit fit, marked 'fit' (weak).

INCREMENTALITY factors are ASSUMPTIONS until tested (brand search 0.30, generic search 0.80, shopping/PMax 0.70, Meta prospecting/Kuling 0.60, retargeting 0.30). Brand Shopping takes the brand rate. Incremental marginal = marginal × factor; incremental GP3 per extra 10 k = (incremental marginal − 1) × 10 k.

Meta marginal: 28-day spend/revenue fit per market × type (or the average ROAS as an upper bound when the fit is weak) × Funnel GP2 margin of that market × incrementality. The approved 200 k plan is the starting point, not a cap. CAUTION: Meta pixel value runs several times above what GA4 last click credits Meta (compare the last-click GP2 ROAS column), so a 0.6 incrementality on pixel value may be generous; treat 'scale up' as a test until a lift test sets the factor.
Meta = warehouse (agg_daily_kpis_by_ad, SEK). ROAS/CPA are platform-reported: Meta pixel purchase value (revenue, not profit) under Meta's own attribution.

Meta campaign type is classified from the campaign name (rules shown with the table). 'Kuling-catalog' counts as Kuling, not catalog retargeting; 'mktcontrib' campaigns are brand-funded and kept outside the plan.
Product / brand / category view covers catalog (DPA) delivery only — Meta reports product breakdowns for catalog ads, not for single-image/video ads.

GP3 = GP2 from the Funnel export (Norce has no cost data, so margins can only come from there), attributed to channel by GA4 last click, − de-duplicated cost, Babyshop shop. Last-click under-credits Meta's view-through effect. Actual sales per market are Norce ordered revenue (refresh_daily_perf definition: Stockholm day, ex VAT, gross of returns, every status except 6); paid COS = Google + Meta spend ÷ Norce merchandise revenue.

Marginal ROAS is an ESTIMATE: log-log fit of daily GP2 vs spend over the last 28 days, slope × average ROAS. Demand moves spend and return together, so it flatters; use it to rank where the next krona goes, not as a forecast. Below 1.0 the last krona loses GP3.
